# MAYA — QA case list

**1649 generated cases across 5 sections**, derived from the source
by `tools/qa/enumerate.py` rather than written from memory. Re-run it after any
wave that adds a route or a refusal; a case list that does not move when the
system does is a case list nobody should trust.

Each case states its **expectation before it runs** — `accepted`, `refused`
with a code, or `reported` — because this platform refuses a great deal on
purpose and a test treating a 409 as a failure has misunderstood the product.

The generator guarantees that **nothing is missing**. It cannot judge whether
what is here is worth running, and it does not produce sequences, boundary
values or races — those are written by hand in the sections after the generated
ones.


| Section | Cases |
|---|---|
| A. Every operation, once | 609 |
| B. Required fields | 157 |
| C. Unknown identifiers | 202 |
| D. Every refusal code | 597 |
| E. Screens | 84 |
| **Generated total** | **1649** |

## F. Governance — sequences and judgement

Hand-written cases for registration, the record lifecycle, versions and
promotion, the approval quorum, risk tiering, segregation of duties, and
decommissioning. These are the half a generator cannot produce: orderings,
boundary values, races, re-runs, and the specific ways two controls that are
each correct combine into a hole. Every operation already has a happy-path case
in section A and every mapped refusal code a provocation case in section D, so
nothing here repeats those.

Read `refused (code)` as: the platform says no and the response body's `error`
field is that code. Where the code is written `code TBD` the case names what to
look for instead.

| ID | Area | Case | Expectation | Steps | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-GOV-001 | `registration` | Register the same URN twice in one session | **refused (registry_refused, 409)** | POST /models with urn U; POST /models with urn U again | a register that admits two rows under one URN cannot answer "which model is this" |
| QA-GOV-002 | `registration` | Register two URNs differing only in letter case | **EXPLORATORY** | POST /models urn `maya://model/credit.pd`; POST /models urn `maya://model/Credit.PD` | look for whether `models.one(urn=)` folds case; two rows here means every later lookup is a coin toss |
| QA-GOV-003 | `registration` | Register a URN that is a strict prefix of an existing one | **accepted (201)** | register `maya://model/credit.pd`; register `maya://model/credit.pd.smallbiz` | `{name:path}` route matching must not let the shorter URN swallow requests meant for the longer |
| QA-GOV-004 | `registration` | Register, then immediately submit with no version and no tier | **refused (nothing_to_approve, 409)** | POST /models; POST /models/{name}/submit | the emptiness check must fire before the tier check, or the operator fixes the wrong thing first |
| QA-GOV-005 | `registration` | Register, add a version, submit without assessing | **refused (not_tiered, 409)** | POST /models; POST /models/{name}/versions; POST /models/{name}/submit | approval depth follows the tier, so submitting untiered is choosing your own control depth |
| QA-GOV-006 | `registration` | Register, assess, add a version, submit — the full ordered path | **accepted (200)** | POST /models; POST /models/{name}/versions; POST /models/{name}/assess; POST /models/{name}/submit | the one ordering that works has to work; a platform whose happy path is unreachable is unusable |
| QA-GOV-007 | `registration` | PATCH an editable field on a draft record | **accepted (200)** | POST /models; PATCH /models/{name} with `{"owner": "x"}` | the mutable states must actually be mutable or every record has to be born perfect |
| QA-GOV-008 | `registration` | PATCH `urn` on a draft record | **refused (registry_refused, 409)** | PATCH /models/{name} with `{"urn": "..."}` | the URN is the identity everything else cites; editable identity makes every stored reference a guess |
| QA-GOV-009 | `registration` | PATCH `status` directly, bypassing the state machine | **refused (registry_refused, 409)** | PATCH /models/{name} with `{"status": "attested"}` | a status settable by PATCH makes the whole seven-state machine decoration |
| QA-GOV-010 | `registration` | PATCH `tier` directly | **refused (registry_refused, 409)** | PATCH /models/{name} with `{"tier": 4}` | the tier is a derivation with a stored rationale; a settable tier is a tier with no derivation |
| QA-GOV-011 | `registration` | PATCH with an empty body | **accepted (200), no evidence node** | PATCH /models/{name} with `{}` | an empty change that appends to the chain inflates the audit trail with acts nobody performed |
| QA-GOV-012 | `registration` | PATCH the same field to the same value twice | **accepted (200) twice, two evidence nodes** | PATCH `{"owner":"x"}`; PATCH `{"owner":"x"}` | check the second node records `from: x` so a reader can tell a no-op from a real change |
| QA-GOV-013 | `registration` | Set designations on an **attested** record | **refused (record_frozen, 409) — EXPECTED TO FAIL** | attest a model; PUT /models/{name}/designations with `["sox_relevant"]` | `catalogue.designate` never consults the lifecycle gate, so an immutable record gains control obligations with no amendment |
| QA-GOV-014 | `registration` | Set designations twice to the same set | **accepted (200), no second evidence node** | PUT designations `["sox_relevant"]` twice | `designate` short-circuits on an equal set; confirm it compares sorted lists, not list order |
| QA-GOV-015 | `registration` | Set designations to `[]` after they were populated | **accepted (200)** | PUT `["sox_relevant"]`; PUT `[]` | removing a designation is as consequential as adding one and must leave `was` on the record |
| QA-GOV-016 | `registration` | Designations containing the same value twice | **accepted (200), stored once** | PUT `["sox_relevant","sox_relevant"]` | a duplicated tag that survives inflates `extra_controls` and the required-controls list |
| QA-GOV-017 | `registration` | Register with `legal_entity` empty, then read it as an entity-scoped principal | **refused (out_of_scope, 403)** | register with `legal_entity: ""`; GET as a principal scoped to LE-UK | `Scope.permits` compares `None not in (...)`, so an entity-less model must be invisible to a scoped reader rather than universally visible |
| QA-GOV-018 | `intake` | Register a proposal before it has been triaged | **refused (not_triaged, 409)** | POST /intake; POST /intake/{ref}/register | the three intake questions are the only ones asked before a model exists |
| QA-GOV-019 | `intake` | Triage out of scope, then try to register | **refused (proposal_declined, 409)** | POST /intake/{ref}/triage `in_scope: false`; POST /intake/{ref}/register | reopening a declined proposal would lose the determination and the reasons somebody gave |

| QA-GOV-021 | `intake` | Re-triage a proposal already in `triaged` | **accepted (200), determination overwritten** | triage in scope; triage again with a different sourcing | only `registered` and `declined` are guarded; confirm the evidence chain keeps both determinations |
| QA-GOV-022 | `intake` | Register a proposal onto a URN already in the register | **refused (registry_refused, 409), proposal stays `triaged`** | register model U; triage a proposal; register it as U | the proposal must not be marked `registered` when the model registration failed |
| QA-GOV-023 | `intake` | Triage with an empty rationale | **refused (rationale_required, 422)** | POST /intake/{ref}/triage with `rationale: "  "` | an out-of-scope decision with no reason gets re-litigated every year by somebody who was not there |
| QA-GOV-024 | `baseline` | Amend a `baselined` record | **refused (illegal_transition, 409)** | import a baselined model; POST /models/{name}/amend | `amend` is reachable only from `attested`; baselined is already mutable and the refusal must say so |
| QA-GOV-025 | `baseline` | Retire a `baselined` record with open debt | **accepted (200) — EXPLORATORY** | import a baselined model with gaps; POST /models/{name}/retire | nothing consults the debt register on retirement; establish whether debt should block or merely be reported |
| QA-GOV-026 | `baseline` | Submit a `baselined` record with open debt | **accepted (200) — EXPLORATORY** | import a baselined model; add a version; assess; submit | if debt does not gate submission then the import's "governed going forward" promise rests entirely on reporting |
| QA-GOV-027 | `baseline` | Import the same legacy model twice from the same source | **refused (registry_refused, 409)** | run the importer twice over one manifest | a re-runnable import must be idempotent or a second sweep doubles the estate |
| QA-GOV-028 | `baseline` | Record the same debt gap twice against one model | **refused (already_recorded, 409)** | raise debt for gap G; raise debt for gap G again | two open debts for one gap makes "what is still owed" a number with two answers |
| QA-GOV-029 | `lifecycle` | Submit twice | **refused (illegal_transition, 409) on the second** | submit; submit again | the refusal must list the legal moves from `submitted`, not merely say no |

| QA-GOV-034 | `lifecycle` | Retire a `submitted` record | **refused (illegal_transition, 409)** | submit; POST /models/{name}/retire | `retire` is reachable from attested, approved, draft and baselined only; finish what is in flight first |

## G. Features, parameters and execution — sequences and judgement

**493 judgement cases**, written by hand against `core/features/`, `core/parameters/`, `core/execution/` and the help pages that promise what they do. They are the half a generator cannot produce: **orderings, boundary values, races, and the combinations in which a control that is right on its own is wrong beside another one.**

`docs/QA/QA-CASES.md` already guarantees that nothing is *missing* — every operation once, every required field, every unknown identifier, every mapped refusal code, every screen. Nothing here duplicates that. Assume each operation below already has a happy path and each refusal code already has one provocation; what is written here is the **second** call, the one made in a particular order, at a particular value, or after something else moved underneath it.

Every case states its expectation **before it runs** — `accepted`, `refused` with a code, or `reported`. MAYA refuses a great deal on purpose and a test treating a 409 as a failure has misunderstood the product. Where the code could not be established from the source it is written `refused (code TBD)` and the case says what to look for. `EXPLORATORY` marks a case whose expectation cannot honestly be stated in advance — each one says what would make the outcome a defect.

Every case is **re-runnable**. The second run is where the state bugs live, and a case that only passes once proves nothing about a real deployment.

| QA-FX-401 | `execution boundary` | The same input under `clamp` | **EXPLORATORY** — expect the value clamped to 20; nothing in the engine clamps | Set `on_boundary_violation: clamp`; execute with `dscr: 91`; read the value the runtime received and the response | the engine only branches on `reject`, so `clamp` behaves exactly like `flag` — a version whose contract says values are clamped is served the raw out-of-range value, and the response is indistinguishable from the flag case |
| QA-FX-402 | `execution boundary` | Exactly at the minimum and exactly at the maximum | **accepted** both — the bounds are inclusive | Execute with `dscr: 0` and `dscr: 20` | an exclusive bound here would refuse the endpoint values a contract was written to permit |
| QA-FX-403 | `execution boundary` | One epsilon below the minimum | **refused** under `reject` | Execute with `dscr: -1e-9` | the other side of the boundary |
| QA-FX-404 | `execution boundary` | An `allowed` list with the value present, then absent | **accepted** then **refused** | Contract `product in [mtg, btl]`; execute with each and then with `cards` | the categorical form of the same bound, and a separate code path |
| QA-FX-405 | `execution boundary` | An assumption whose key no input supplies | **accepted**, logged as unchecked, and **reported** — `boundary_ok` is `true` | Contract a bound on `ltv`; execute supplying only `dscr`; read the response and the log | the boundary held and the boundary never applied look identical from `boundary_ok` alone, and the second is what a silently unenforced contract looks like from outside |
| QA-FX-406 | `execution boundary` | A contract section spelled `assumption` | **refused** at version registration, naming the known keys | Register a version with `contract: {assumption: [...]}` | the whole section would vanish and the version would read as governed and not be |
| QA-FX-407 | `execution boundary` | `min` and `max` instead of `minimum` and `maximum` | **refused** at registration | Register with `{key: dscr, min: 0, max: 20}` | the clause survives with no bounds at all, so `dscr` constrained to [0, 20] admits anything |
| QA-FX-408 | `execution boundary` | A minimum above the maximum | **refused** at registration | Register with `{key: dscr, minimum: 20, maximum: 0}` | an admissible region no input can satisfy, which L-7 nonetheless compares between two versions |
| QA-FX-409 | `execution boundary` | A clause with no `key` | **refused** at registration, naming the clause; not a 500 | Register with `{minimum: 0, maximum: 20}` | a raw `KeyError` out of `bounds_of` is a 500 where a refusal belongs |
| QA-FX-410 | `execution boundary` | An unknown `on_boundary_violation` value | **refused** at registration, naming the three | Register with `on_boundary_violation: warn` | an unrecognised policy would fall through to whatever the default branch does |
| QA-FX-411 | `execution boundary` | Two empty contracts compared under L-7 | **EXPLORATORY** — refinement between two contracts that pin nothing holds vacuously | Register two versions each with `contract: {}`; promote one over the other | the alias gate would report a refinement that constrains nothing |

| QA-FX-413 | `execution` | An implemented runtime whose dependency is missing | **refused** — 503 `runtime_unavailable`, naming the package | Uninstall onnxruntime; execute an ONNX warrant | same, on the other side |
| QA-FX-414 | `execution` | An artifact whose digest does not match the warrant | **refused** — `artifact_mismatch`, before the artifact is loaded | Approve an artifact; overwrite the file; execute | this is the point at which the whole chain either does or does not describe the bytes about to run |

| QA-FX-416 | `execution` | An artifact path resolving outside the configured root | **refused** — `artifact_outside_root` | Execute a warrant whose `realisation.uri` is `../../etc/passwd` | treating a path inside a document from elsewhere as trustworthy turns a governance system into a file-read primitive |
| QA-FX-417 | `execution` | An artifact the store does not hold | **refused** — `artifact_missing` or `no_artifact` | Execute against a digest nobody uploaded | distinct from a mismatch, and the remediation differs |

| QA-FX-427 | `execution` | The engine holds no reference to the registry or the feature store | **accepted** — asserted by construction | Inspect the engine's constructor arguments and the test that pins them | a boundary is only real if it is enforced by construction rather than by intention |
| QA-FX-428 | `execution` | PMML `RegressionModel` and `Scorecard` | **accepted** — evaluated natively, no JVM | Execute one of each | the two element types covering most of a bank's PMML estate |

| QA-FX-430 | `execution` | A PMML normalisation method outside the four | **refused** by name | Execute a `RegressionModel` with `normalizationMethod: probit` | a normalisation silently swapped moves every score |

| QA-FX-436 | `execution` | A malformed curve, date and fixing | **refused** — three distinct codes | Execute one warrant per malformation | each named rather than substituted |
| QA-FX-437 | `execution` | A curve of one point | **EXPLORATORY** — a single-point curve either prices flat or refuses | Price a discount factor against a one-point curve | a flat curve produced from insufficient data is a number with no market behind it |

| QA-FX-448 | `warrant profiles` | A profile with no defaults | **refused** — `empty_profile` | POST with `defaults: {}` | it would do nothing and read as if it did something |

| QA-FX-464 | `shadow` | A shadow grant whose declared use is a production use | **refused** — `shadow_use_is_a_production_use` | Create a shadow grant using the model's approved production use | otherwise a shadow is a way to obtain production authority without the approval |
| QA-FX-465 | `zones` | A zone that may not hold the data class | **refused** — `zone_may_not_hold_this_data`, naming the class | Execute a model reading `restricted` data in a zone permitted only to `internal` | the class propagates from the features, so this is where the propagation either bites or does not |
| QA-FX-466 | `zones` | A purpose not permitted in the zone | **refused** — `purpose_not_permitted_in_zone` | Execute with a declared use whose purpose class the zone does not admit | data collected for one purpose reused for another is the failure the zone exists to prevent |
| QA-FX-467 | `runs` | A verb outside the ten | **refused** — `unknown_verb`, naming the ten | Open a run with `verb: train` | a run and the warrant authorising it must not be able to describe the same act differently |
| QA-FX-468 | `runs` | A duplicate run reference | **refused** — `run_already_open` | Open two runs called `sweep-1` | two runs under one name is a training record that cannot be read |
| QA-FX-469 | `runs` | A child of a closed parent | **refused** — `parent_closed` | Close the parent; open a child | a child starting now would be outside the search it belongs to |
| QA-FX-470 | `runs` | A grandchild | **refused** — `nesting_too_deep` | Open a child of a child | the child count is the number that makes a sweep readable |
| QA-FX-471 | `runs` | Closing a closed run | **refused** — `run_closed` | Close twice | a run closes once; a second activity is a second run |
| QA-FX-472 | `runs` | Closing as `lost` | **refused** — `unknown_outcome`; `lost` is derived from the clock | Close with `state: lost` | a caller marking their own run lost would erase the distinction between abandoned and timed out |
| QA-FX-473 | `runs` | Closing as failed with no note | **refused** — `note_required` | Close with `state: failed` and no note | the failures are the part of a training record anybody ever reads twice |
| QA-FX-474 | `retraining` | A policy with no trigger | **refused** — `trigger_required` | POST a retraining policy with `triggers: []` | better said by not having a policy |
| QA-FX-475 | `retraining` | An unknown trigger | **refused** — `unknown_trigger`, naming the five | POST with `triggers: ['vibes']` | a trigger MAYA cannot compute is a standing approval nothing will ever fire |
| QA-FX-476 | `retraining` | A standing approval with no rationale | **refused** — `rationale_required` | POST with no rationale | it delegates a judgement, and the person reading it in a year was not in the room |
| QA-FX-477 | `retraining` | Automatic acceptance on a Tier 1 model | **refused** — `tier_not_eligible` | POST an auto-accept policy for a Tier 1 model | tier 1 may never accept a parameter set without a person |
| QA-FX-478 | `retraining` | Automatic acceptance with no tolerance | **refused** — `tolerance_required` | POST auto-accept with no declared tolerance | a tolerance evaluated by whatever happens to read it is not a tolerance |
| QA-FX-479 | `retraining` | The author approving their own standing approval | **refused** — `author_may_not_approve` | Write and approve as one actor | it delegates a judgement over every future re-fit of this model |
| QA-FX-480 | `training records` | A fitted set with no warrant | **reported** — the authority section is a named gap, not a blank heading | Record a fitted set through a path that admits no warrant; preview its training record | a heading with nothing under it reads as an omission; a named gap reads as a fact |
| QA-FX-481 | `training records` | Preview authors nothing | **accepted** — nothing is filed | GET the preview; list documents for the subject | compiled rather than written is the claim, and a preview that filed would break it |
| QA-FX-482 | `training records` | Filing the same training record twice | **EXPLORATORY** — expect a second version or a refusal, never a silent replacement | POST `/api/v1/training-records/{id}` twice | a document that changes under a fixed identifier is the failure the pinned subject kinds exist to prevent |
| QA-FX-483 | `training records` | A training record over an out-of-line parameter set | **reported** — the values section says where they are held, with the cardinality | Record with `values_uri`; compile the record | a record that showed nothing under what it produced would read as an empty fit |
| QA-FX-484 | `dossier` | A dossier for a model with nothing filed | **reported** — every node a named gap with what was expected | GET `/api/v1/dossiers/{name}` for a fresh model | a reader cannot tell a thin model from a thin page unless the page says which it is |
| QA-FX-485 | `dossier` | The dossier is computed, never stored | **accepted** — filing a document changes the dossier with no refresh step | GET the dossier; attach a document; GET again | a stored dossier would be a second account of the documentation, able to disagree with the first |
| QA-FX-486 | `dossier` | A document filed against a `featureset` rather than a `featureset_version` | **refused** — the vocabulary has six subject kinds and `featureset` is not one | POST an attachment with `subject_kind: featureset` | a document filed against the set would describe something that has since moved |
| QA-FX-487 | `dossier` | Two exports of the same dossier state | **accepted** — byte-identical, digested member by member | Export the pack twice with no intervening change; compare digests | an export that is not reproducible cannot be handed to somebody who will never be given a login |
| QA-FX-488 | `re-runnability` | Every case in this section runs twice | **accepted** — the second run gives the same outcome, or a named `already exists` | Run the whole section against one estate twice | the second run is where state bugs live, and a suite that only passes once proves nothing about a real deployment |
| QA-FX-489 | `re-runnability` | The whole featureset-to-parameter cycle walked by four different people | **accepted** — no single account can complete it | Define as a data engineer, publish as a steward, fit as a model developer, approve as second line; then attempt the same walk as one account | a test that does everything as `admin` proves nothing about segregation of duties |
| QA-FX-490 | `boundaries` | An empty estate | **reported** — every features, parameters and warrant list answers with zero and says so | Start a fresh instance; GET every list route in this section | a count of zero and a route that failed must not look the same |
| QA-FX-491 | `boundaries` | One feature, one view, one version, one slot, one row | **accepted** — the whole path completes | Walk define, materialise, publish, assemble, fit, approve, execute at N=1 throughout | the smallest estate is where every aggregate divides by something |
| QA-FX-492 | `boundaries` | A featureset whose only slot is its label | **EXPLORATORY** — the schema excludes the label, so the set provides nothing | Declare one slot, name it the label slot, publish, then issue a fit warrant | `schema()` filters the label out, so a one-slot supervised set satisfies a kernel that reads nothing and refuses every other |
| QA-FX-493 | `boundaries` | A contract binding nothing and a warrant reading it | **EXPLORATORY** — an empty contract makes L-17 hold vacuously | Bind an empty contract; attest; read the agreement | a law that holds because there was nothing to check must report that, not agreement |

## H. Validation, findings and monitoring — sequences and judgement

The generated list in `docs/QA/QA-CASES.md` guarantees that no operation, no
required field, no unknown identifier and no mapped refusal code is *missing*.
It cannot tell whether a control that is right on its own is still right in
combination, and it produces no orderings, no boundary values and no second
runs. These are the cases it cannot write.

Every expectation is stated before the case runs, as `accepted`, `refused
(code)` or `reported`. **`reported` carries most of the weight here**: this half
of the platform mostly raises findings rather than refusing, and a case whose
expectation is "a finding appears, with these words in it" is as much a control
as a 409. Where a code is not knowable from the source without running the
instance it is written `refused (code TBD)` with what to look for.

Run every case twice. The second run is where the state bugs are.

| ID | Area | Case | Expectation | Steps | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-AM-001 | Validation episode | Independence when the builder's name is spelled differently: version created by `d.raman`, validator named `person/d.raman` | **refused (`validation_refused`, 409 — independence failed)** | 1. Create a version authenticating as `d.raman`. 2. POST /validations with validators `["person/d.raman"]`. | this comparison was once `==`, so the control was inert over HTTP while its unit test passed |
| QA-AM-002 | Validation episode | Independence with the case flipped: validator named `PERSON/D.Raman` | **refused (`validation_refused`, 409)** | As QA-AM-001 with the validator upper-cased. | a duties check that is case-sensitive is a duties check with a shift key for a bypass |
| QA-AM-003 | Validation episode | Two validators, one of whom built the version | **refused (`validation_refused`, 409), and no episode is created** | 1. POST /validations with `["person/a.mehta", "person/d.raman"]`. 2. GET /validations for the model and confirm the count is unchanged. | adding an independent name beside a conflicted one must not launder the conflicted one |
| QA-AM-004 | Validation episode | Validator who resolves to nobody | **refused (`validation_refused`, 409 — no principal registered)** | POST /validations with validators `["person/nobody.at.all"]`. | independence tested against a name that resolves to nobody passes by construction |
| QA-AM-005 | Validation episode | Validator who exists but is not active | **refused (`validation_refused`, 409 — not active)** | 1. Deactivate a principal. 2. Open an episode naming them. | a challenge recorded against a departed person is not a record of who challenged |
| QA-AM-006 | Validation episode | Validator deactivated *after* the episode opened, then the episode is concluded | **accepted, and nothing reports it** | 1. Open an episode naming an active validator. 2. Deactivate them. 3. Conclude. | validators are resolved at open and never again; decide whether that silence is intended before a supervisor finds it |
| QA-AM-007 | Validation episode | Version with no recorded `created_by` at all | **accepted — independence passes by construction** | 1. Create a version by a path that leaves `created_by` empty. 2. Open an episode with any validator. | `attest()` finds no conflict when there is no builder, so an unattributed version is independently validated by everybody |
| QA-AM-008 | Validation episode | Two episodes open on one version at once, concluded to opposite outcomes | **both accepted** | 1. Open episode A and episode B on `3.2.1`. 2. Conclude A `rejected`, B `approved`. | nothing refuses a second concurrent episode; the model page must not be able to show one and hide the other |
| QA-AM-009 | Validation episode | Conclude with no `tier_verdict` | **refused (`validation_refused`, 409)** | POST /conclude with `{"outcome": "approved"}` only. | not looking at the tier is not a verdict, and it used to read exactly like agreeing |
| QA-AM-010 | Validation episode | Conclude `should_be_higher` with a note of a single space | **refused (`validation_refused`, 409)** | POST /conclude with `tier_note: " "`. | a whitespace note satisfies a truthiness check and tells the re-assessor nothing |
| QA-AM-011 | Validation episode | Conclude `should_be_higher`; the finding it raises is owned by the first named validator | **accepted, and reported: a finding appears owned by `validators[0]`** | 1. Conclude with `should_be_higher` and a note. 2. GET /findings for the model. | the validator now owns a finding they may not close; confirm the handover route is obvious from the finding |
| QA-AM-012 | Validation episode | Conclude `should_be_lower` | **accepted, and no finding is raised** | Conclude with `should_be_lower` and a note; list findings. | a request to reduce control belongs in a signed re-assessment, not in a remediation queue |
| QA-AM-013 | Validation episode | Model is re-tiered from 3 to 1 between open and conclude, then concluded `remains_appropriate` | **accepted, and reported: `tier_at_open` is 3** | 1. Open. 2. Re-assess to tier 1. 3. Conclude `remains_appropriate`. 4. Read the episode. | the verdict is unreadable without the tier the validator was looking at; check the reading says which |
| QA-AM-014 | Validation episode | Conclude `approved` with no test result recorded at all | **refused (`validation_refused`, 409 — nothing this validation examined)** | Open, then conclude `approved` immediately. | an episode with no results has an empty failed list, which satisfied every other check |

| QA-AM-227 | Evaluation and breaches | Evaluate from telemetry on a monitor bound to no version | **refused (`monitor_has_no_version`)** | Define without `model_version_id`, then evaluate from telemetry. | a monitor with no version has no telemetry stream, and guessing one would monitor the wrong population |
| QA-AM-228 | Evaluation and breaches | Evaluate from telemetry on an instance with no collector | **refused (`no_telemetry`)** | Wire a service with no collector and call the endpoint. | an absent capability must refuse rather than read an empty cohort |
| QA-AM-229 | Evaluation and breaches | `monitor:observe` holder attempts to evaluate | **refused (403)** | Authenticate as the `service` role and POST /evaluate. | the principal that runs the model holds the population; it must not also rule on it |

| QA-AM-237 | Telemetry | Deliver with `sample_rate: 0` | **refused (`bad_sample_rate`)** | POST with a rate of zero. | a rate of zero is not a proportion, and it would make every extrapolation infinite |

<!-- I-platform-interfaces.md -->
## I. Platform, interfaces and operations — sequences and judgement

`docs/QA/QA-CASES.md` holds 1,636 cases generated from the source: every
operation once, every required-field refusal, every unknown-identifier 404,
every mapped refusal code, and every navbar screen against a role that should
see it and one that should not. Those guarantee nothing is **missing**.

This file is the half a generator cannot produce. Every case here is a
**sequence**, a **boundary**, a **race**, or a **combination** — a control that
is right on its own and wrong beside another one. Nothing here repeats a
generated case: where a case names an operation the generator already covers, it
is the *second* call, the *stale* header, the *concurrent* writer or the
*restored* instance that is being tested, never the happy path.

**Every expectation is stated before the case runs**, as `accepted`,
`refused (code)` or `reported`. `refused (code TBD)` means the refusal is
required and the code has not been read out of the source yet — that is a case
outcome to record, not a case to skip.

**Three house rules apply to every case below.**

1. **A refusal is usually the feature working.** A 409, a 412 or a 423 that
   carries `error`, `detail` and `remediation` is a pass when the case predicted
   it. What is reportable is the opposite: a success that corresponds to nothing.
2. **A screen case must prove it got the page it asked for.** The interface
   ignores HTTP Basic and answers **200 with the sign-in page**, which has
   already fooled one test pass. Asserting `200` proves nothing. Assert on
   `href="/logout"` in the body — present only when a session is established —
   and on the page's own `<title>`. `403` renders `forbidden.html`, whose title
   is `Not available to you`, the only page title in the product that omits
   ` — MAYA`.
3. **Mark the environment.** Cases tagged **[PG]** need
   `database.url: postgresql+psycopg://…`; **[ICEBERG]** need
   `data.table_format: iceberg` (or `MAYA_TABLE_FORMAT=iceberg`, which wins over
   the file). A previous pass could run neither and said so. Untagged cases run
   on the SQLite/Delta default.

Estate under test is the one `docs/QA/qa_setup.py` builds — model
`maya://model/qa.pd.scorecard` at `1.0.0`, principals `admin`, `q.tester`,
`s.iqbal`, `j.okafor`, `a.mehta`, `d.raman`, `svc/qa-runner`. Run the instance
on a non-default port with a config in a temporary directory, never against the
repository's own `data/`.

**400 judgement cases**, in ID order by domain.

| IDs | Domain | Cases |
|---|---|---|
| QA-PLT-001 – 040 | the evidence chain, the checkpoint, anchors, WORM, timestamps | 40 |
| QA-PLT-041 – 122 | persistence — transactions, idempotency, ETags, the estate fold, immutability, row-level security, dialects and table formats (with 17 more evidence cases the persistence findings opened up) | 82 |
| QA-PLT-123 – 179 | documents — compilation, the graph, dossiers, review, packs and shares, search and its coverage figure | 57 |
| QA-PLT-180 – 217 | machine assistance — tiers, the oracle, grounding, citations, unverified narrative, budgets, canaries, probes, injection | 38 |
| QA-PLT-218 – 256 | operations — backup and restore, the scheduler, notifications and subscriptions | 39 |
| QA-PLT-257 – 296 | plugins, discovery and the scanner contract, rule import, migrations | 40 |

| QA-PLT-288 | rules | A rule set of 513 rules | **refused (`too_many_rules`)** at 513 and **accepted** at 512 | publish both | both sides of the bound |

| QA-PLT-300 | configuration | Malformed YAML | **refused** (the process does not start, naming the file and the parse error) | corrupt the config file; start | the case is here to pin the one configuration fault that is fatal, next to the one that is not |

| QA-PLT-310 | health | `/health/ready` with schema drift, a dead notifier and a stopped scheduler | **accepted (200 ready)** — and each named in the body | arrange all three; probe | readiness deliberately gates on two things only; the case makes the other three visible so nobody assumes they are covered |
| QA-PLT-311 | health | `/health/encryption` on a default instance | **reported** (every finding that is not what a production instance should have) | read it on the QA instance | the platform does not encrypt and does not pretend to; the posture must not read as a tick |

| QA-PLT-375 | cli | An answer containing a nested list of more than twenty objects | **reported** (the output says how many were not printed) — predicted: it prints twenty and says nothing | run a command whose answer carries 25 nested rows, with and without `--json` | a CLI that silently truncates is a CLI whose output cannot be used as evidence of anything |
| QA-PLT-376 | cli | Answers on stdout, refusals on stderr | **accepted** | pipe stdout to a file for a successful and a refused command; check each stream | a pipeline capturing stdout must not silently capture a refusal as data |
| QA-PLT-377 | sdk | A client built with no credentials | **refused** at construction, before any call | construct `Maya(base_url=...)` with nothing else | a client that constructs and then fails at the first call sends an operator looking at the network |
| QA-PLT-378 | sdk | A POST that times out | **refused (`Unreachable`)** after exactly one attempt | make a POST time out and count the requests that reached the server | retrying a POST would double a governance act; the case proves it is not retried |
| QA-PLT-379 | sdk | A GET that times out twice and then succeeds | **accepted** (three attempts, exponential backoff) | fail the first two attempts | idempotent methods retry and the rest do not; both halves need a case |
| QA-PLT-380 | sdk | A 500 from the server | **refused (`Refused`)** — never retried | return a 500 and count attempts | HTTP errors are answers; retrying one hides a server that is failing every time |
| QA-PLT-381 | sdk | A refusal returned rather than raised | **refused (raised)** — every status at or above 400 raises | drive one refusal per status class and assert the exception class | a client that returns a refusal as data is a client whose caller will use the data |
| QA-PLT-382 | sdk | The exception class for each refusal class | **refused** — 401, 403, 404, 409, 410 and 423 map to named classes; 412, 422, 428, 429 and every 5xx are a plain `Refused` | provoke one of each and assert the class | a rate limit and a lock are different situations and are currently different classes; a precondition failure and a validation error are not |
| QA-PLT-383 | sdk | A proxy returning an HTML 502 | **refused** with a synthetic code and the body preserved | put an HTML-returning proxy in front and call anything | a refusal shape invented from a non-problem body must be recognisable as invented |
| QA-PLT-384 | sdk | The request id round trip | **accepted** (the id the client sent, or the server's, readable afterwards) | make a call; read `last_request_id`; find that id in the live log | this is how a defect report becomes reproducible |
| QA-PLT-385 | notebook | A refusal raised inside a notebook | **refused** (rendered as HTML **and** re-raised) | install the handler in a stub shell; raise a refusal; check both the render and that the exception propagated | a scheduled notebook must still fail; only what a person sees first changes |
| QA-PLT-386 | notebook | An unreachable platform inside a notebook | **refused**, rendered differently from a refusal, and never containing the word `REFUSED` | raise an unreachable error through the handler | the two must not look alike on a screen, for the same reason they are two exit codes |
| QA-PLT-387 | notebook | A refusal whose detail contains HTML | **accepted** (escaped) | raise a refusal whose detail contains a script tag | a refusal is text from the platform, and a notebook that renders it as markup is an injection surface in an analyst's browser |
| QA-PLT-388 | notebook | An empty result rendered as a table | **reported** ("nothing to show — which is not the same as nothing existing") | render an empty list | an empty table in a notebook is read as *there is nothing*, and it usually means *you were scoped to nothing* |
| QA-PLT-389 | notebook | The module outside a notebook | **accepted** (installs nothing, returns false, imports no IPython) | import and install with no shell present | a client library that imports a notebook framework is a client library that cannot be installed in a service |
| QA-PLT-390 | accessibility | Every screen at the largest text scale | **reported** (no horizontal overflow, no clipped control, every action reachable) | set the text scale to largest; walk the 42 screens at a 1280px and a 320px viewport | the help page claims a wide table stays a wide table with larger type in it, and nothing in the suite has ever rendered a page to check |
| QA-PLT-391 | accessibility | The widest governance tables at the largest scale | **reported** | at largest, load the principals, portfolio and estate screens and look for a page body that scrolls sideways | wide tables and a 33-element navbar are the plausible break points, and they are the screens people live in |
| QA-PLT-392 | accessibility | Each of the five appearance choices, applied and reloaded | **accepted** (the choice survives a reload with no flash of the other theme) | select each of the three modes and two palettes in turn; reload; observe the first paint | the pre-paint script and the picker are two implementations of one decision, and they can drift |
| QA-PLT-393 | accessibility | An invalid theme value pushed through the public API | **accepted** (no change, no broken state) — never a half-applied theme | call the theme setter with a value that is not one of the five | a theme picker that accepts anything leaves a page with an attribute no stylesheet answers |
| QA-PLT-394 | accessibility | A theme chosen in one browser and the same account in another | **reported** (the choice is per browser, not per account) | sign in as one principal in two browsers and set different themes | this is stated in the help and is the kind of thing a support call is made of |
| QA-PLT-395 | accessibility | Keyboard-only, from the address bar to the primary action, on ten screens | **accepted** (the skip link is the first stop, focus is always visible, and the primary action is reachable) | tab through without touching the mouse | the sortable table headers make every column a tab stop, so some screens have forty stops before the content |
| QA-PLT-396 | accessibility | The focus ring on a crimson surface | **accepted** (inverted and visible) in all five appearance choices | tab onto a navbar link, a table header and the danger button under each theme | a focus ring that matches the surface it sits on is a focus ring that is not there |
| QA-PLT-397 | accessibility | The badge and menu contrast in the two named palettes | **accepted** (every text pair clears the AA bar) | measure the badge and dropdown colours under both palettes | the palettes were added after the contrast rules and are the most likely place a token was forgotten |
| QA-PLT-398 | accessibility | A screen under reduced motion | **accepted** (no animation runs) | set the operating system preference and load a screen with transitions | the rule is asserted today by checking the stylesheet contains a string, which proves it was written and not that it applies |
| QA-PLT-399 | accessibility | An outcome announced to a screen reader | **accepted** (the live region updates and is announced) | perform a write on the principals screen and on the warrant author screen with a screen reader running | eighteen templates declare live regions and nothing has ever heard one |
| QA-PLT-400 | accessibility | The sign-in page and the 403 page under every theme and the largest scale | **accepted** | render both at largest scale in all five appearance choices | these are the two pages a locked-out or newly-onboarded person meets first, and neither is on anybody's screenshot list |


<!-- J-deletion-and-storage.md -->
## J. Deletion, tombstones and storage reclamation

Hand-written cases for the one act with no workflow, no reversal and no second
signature — and for the two things that happen around it: the cascade over the
other thirty-seven tables carrying a `model_id`, and the reclamation of bytes
nothing references any more.

**The failure this section is really about is not a failed deletion.** It is a
*successful* one followed by a registration. Delete `pd-retail`, register a new
model called `pd-retail`, and every evidence node, closed finding and amendment
naming that URN now reads as though it described the new model. `verify_chain`
passes throughout, because the chain is intact — it is simply about something
else, and no integrity check that operates on hashes can ever see that. Cases
QA-DEL-020 through QA-DEL-027 are that attack.

The second theme is the one that produced this subsystem: **a reference check
that misses a table does not fail, it approves.** Four tables were never read,
and the test guarding against exactly that passed because their names appeared
in prose. Cases QA-DEL-040 onward walk every disposition.

| ID | Area | Case | Expectation | Steps | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA-DEL-001 | `deletion` | Delete as a non-administrator holding `model:delete` | **refused (deletion_refused, 403)** | grant `model:delete` to a non-admin role; DELETE /models/{name} | the role is checked as well as the permission, so a mistaken grant has to be made twice |
| QA-DEL-002 | `deletion` | Delete with an empty reason | **refused (reason_required, 422)** | DELETE /models/{name} with `reason=""` | an irreversible act with no stated cause is unauditable afterwards |
| QA-DEL-003 | `deletion` | Delete with a whitespace-only reason | **refused (reason_required, 422)** | DELETE with `reason="   "` | `.strip()` must be applied, or the check is decorative |
| QA-DEL-004 | `deletion` | Delete a model covered by a model-scoped legal hold | **refused (under_legal_hold, 423)** | place a hold scoped to the model; DELETE | deleting through a hold is spoliation |
| QA-DEL-005 | `deletion` | Delete a model covered by an estate-wide hold | **refused (under_legal_hold, 423)** | place an estate hold; DELETE any model | an estate hold is a blunt instrument on purpose |
| QA-DEL-006 | `deletion` | Delete a model whose hold was placed by URN rather than id | **refused (under_legal_hold, 423)** | place a hold with `scope_id` = the model's URN; DELETE | this was a real defect: the hold resolved against `model_id` and a URN never matched, so the hold was inert |
| QA-DEL-007 | `deletion` | Delete after the covering hold is lifted | **accepted (200)** | place hold; lift with reason; DELETE | a lifted hold must actually stop refusing |
| QA-DEL-008 | `deletion` | Look for a `force` or `override` parameter on delete | **refused / absent** | read the OpenAPI for DELETE /models/{name} | a hold a deletion could step over would not be a hold |
| QA-DEL-009 | `deletion` | Delete a model that does not exist | **refused (404)** | DELETE /models/no-such-model | must not be the same answer as a successful deletion of nothing |
| QA-DEL-010 | `deletion` | Delete the same model twice | **refused (404 on the second)** | DELETE; DELETE again | the second call must not report success |
| QA-DEL-011 | `deletion` | Confirm the evidence node is appended before the rows go | **accepted; node present** | DELETE; GET the evidence chain filtered to `model_deleted` | a removal that fails halfway must still record who intended it |
| QA-DEL-012 | `deletion` | Verify the chain after a deletion | **reported valid** | DELETE; POST /evidence/verify | the chain survives the deletion by design |
| QA-DEL-013 | `deletion` | Delete on a deployment with no tombstone register wired | **refused (no_tombstone_register, 501)** | construct `LifecycleService` without `tombstones=`; call `delete` | degrading to a deletion that frees the URN is worse than failing |
| QA-DEL-014 | `deletion` | Read the `destroyed` counts on the deletion response | **accepted; counts present** | attach limitations and assumptions; DELETE; read `destroyed` | after the cascade there is nothing left to count |
| QA-DEL-015 | `deletion` | Confirm the response says storage was NOT reclaimed | **accepted; `storage_reclaimed` false** | DELETE; read the response | the bytes are a separate act, and saying otherwise is a claim the platform has not earned |
| QA-DEL-020 | `tombstone` | Register a model at a URN that belonged to a deleted one | **refused (urn_was_deleted, 409)** | register `pd-retail`; DELETE it; register `pd-retail` again | the whole reason the table exists |
| QA-DEL-021 | `tombstone` | Read the refusal's detail for the date and the actor | **refused; detail names both** | as above; read `detail` | somebody told *no* picks another name; somebody told *this belonged to a model Ana destroyed in March* knows whether that is a problem |
| QA-DEL-022 | `tombstone` | Register at a URN that never existed | **accepted (201)** | register a fresh name | a URN free because nobody used it is not a URN free because somebody destroyed what used it |
| QA-DEL-023 | `tombstone` | GET /tombstones/{urn} for a deleted model | **accepted; `deleted` true** | DELETE; GET /tombstones/{urn} | a historical reference must resolve to *there was one* rather than to nothing |
| QA-DEL-024 | `tombstone` | GET /tombstones/{urn} for a URN nobody ever used | **refused (no_such_urn, 404)** | GET /tombstones/urn:maya:model:never | conflating the two is how a mistyped name reads as a deletion |
| QA-DEL-025 | `tombstone` | Confirm the tombstone records the state deleted *from* | **accepted; `status` matches** | delete one model from `draft` and one from `retired`; compare | deleting a draft is housekeeping; deleting a retired model that made decisions for six years is not, and nothing else records which happened |
| QA-DEL-026 | `tombstone` | Confirm a deleted model does not appear in listings | **accepted; absent** | DELETE; GET /models | a tombstone is not a soft delete, and a record alive in one screen and dead in another is the failure mode of that pattern |
| QA-DEL-027 | `tombstone` | Attempt to transition, attest or approve a tombstoned URN | **refused (404 each)** | DELETE; POST each lifecycle transition | the marker carries none of the operational fields |
| QA-DEL-028 | `tombstone` | Look for a route that lifts or reverses a tombstone | **absent** | read the OpenAPI for tombstone paths | restoring would produce an empty model wearing a dead one's identity — the exact confusion the module prevents, arriving through the front door |
| QA-DEL-029 | `tombstone` | GET /tombstones as a principal without `evidence:read` | **refused (403)** | authenticate as a reader without the permission | |
| QA-DEL-040 | `cascade` | Delete a model with an outstanding campaign item | **refused (still_referenced, 409)** | add the model to a campaign; leave the item outstanding; DELETE | a campaign completes when every item is answered; an item naming a deleted model can never be, so the campaign never completes through any state a person can see |
| QA-DEL-041 | `cascade` | Delete a model with an *answered* campaign item | **accepted (200)** | answer the item; DELETE | historical references must not block, or the control is unusable |
| QA-DEL-042 | `cascade` | Delete a model with an unfinished validation | **refused (still_referenced, 409)** | open a validation; DELETE | verified defect: reported `deletable: true` with zero references |
| QA-DEL-043 | `cascade` | Delete a model with a version approval still being collected | **refused (still_referenced, 409)** | open an approval; DELETE | same defect, same cause — the table was never read |
| QA-DEL-044 | `cascade` | Delete a model with a live control waiver | **refused (still_referenced, 409)** | raise a waiver; DELETE | deleting would retire the compensating control with nothing recording that it lapsed |
| QA-DEL-045 | `cascade` | Delete a model with an undischarged approval condition | **refused (still_referenced, 409)** | impose a condition; DELETE | |
| QA-DEL-046 | `cascade` | Delete a model with an export share still readable outside the firm | **refused (still_referenced, 409)** | create a share; DELETE | deleting the model does not withdraw the share |
| QA-DEL-047 | `cascade` | Delete a model with an open breach | **refused (still_referenced, 409)** | breach appetite; DELETE | |
| QA-DEL-048 | `cascade` | Delete a model with an open amendment | **refused (still_referenced, 409)** | open an amendment; DELETE | |
| QA-DEL-049 | `cascade` | Delete a model with an active overlay | **refused (still_referenced, 409)** | apply an overlay; DELETE | |
| QA-DEL-050 | `cascade` | Delete a model with an open elicitation | **refused (still_referenced, 409)** | open an elicitation; DELETE | |
| QA-DEL-051 | `cascade` | Delete a model with an active retrain policy | **refused (still_referenced, 409)** | set a policy; DELETE | |
| QA-DEL-052 | `cascade` | Delete a model with a parallel run in progress | **refused (still_referenced, 409)** | start a parallel run; DELETE | |
| QA-DEL-053 | `cascade` | Confirm the refusal names what refers to it | **refused; detail lists them** | DELETE with three blocking references; read `detail` | somebody told *why* goes and deals with it; somebody told *no* finds another way |
| QA-DEL-054 | `cascade` | Delete a model with limitations and assumptions attached | **accepted; both destroyed** | attach both; DELETE; query the tables | meaningless without the model — dependent, not unimportant |
| QA-DEL-055 | `cascade` | Confirm inference records survive the deletion | **accepted; rows remain** | log an inference; DELETE; query `inference` | a decision the model actually made and somebody relied on is the thing a deletion must not erase |
| QA-DEL-056 | `cascade` | Confirm warrant invocations survive and are counted as kept | **accepted; `(kept)` count present** | invoke; DELETE; read `destroyed` | "nothing was destroyed" and "nothing was there" are different answers |
| QA-DEL-057 | `cascade` | GET /deletion-cascade and compare against the schema | **accepted; 38 rows** | GET; count tables carrying a `model_id` | an operator must not have to discover the disposition by performing it |
| QA-DEL-058 | `cascade` | Add a table with a `model_id` and no disposition | **build fails** | add a column; run `tests/test_tombstones.py` | adding a table must force the decision rather than default to silently unchecked |
| QA-DEL-059 | `cascade` | Confirm a blocking row is never destroyed by the cascade | **accepted; row intact** | force `Cascade.destroy` with a blocking row present; query it | a cascade that could destroy a blocking row would make the refusal decorative |
| QA-DEL-070 | `compaction` | Sweep once with an unreferenced blob present | **accepted; marked, not swept** | write a blob; POST /compaction/sweep; check the file | an upload writes bytes then the row; a sweeper in between sees exactly what an orphan looks like |
| QA-DEL-071 | `compaction` | Sweep twice | **accepted; swept** | POST sweep; POST sweep; check the file | |
| QA-DEL-072 | `compaction` | Add a reference between the two passes | **accepted; mark cleared, blob intact** | sweep; insert a `model_version` naming the digest; sweep twice more | a mark that merely expired would reclaim a live artifact |
| QA-DEL-073 | `compaction` | Two models sharing one checkpoint, delete one | **accepted; blob intact** | two versions on one digest; remove one; sweep twice | content addressing means a per-model delete takes the survivor's bytes |
| QA-DEL-074 | `compaction` | Sweep under an estate-wide legal hold | **refused (under_legal_hold, 423)** | place an estate hold; POST sweep | a refcount says whether bytes are needed; a hold says whether anyone may destroy them, and the first is not an answer to the second |
| QA-DEL-075 | `compaction` | GET /compaction/plan | **accepted; reclaims nothing** | write an orphan; GET plan twice; check the file | the plan must be safe to run repeatedly |
| QA-DEL-076 | `compaction` | POST /compaction/sweep?dry_run=true | **accepted; reports, reclaims nothing** | sweep once; sweep dry; check the file | |
| QA-DEL-077 | `compaction` | Read `not_reclaimable` in the plan | **accepted; Delta bytes and reason** | configure a Delta root with data; GET plan | silently not touching Delta and reporting nothing look identical to an operator staring at disk usage |
| QA-DEL-078 | `compaction` | POST /compaction/vacuum after a cascade | **accepted; file shrinks** | delete a model with many dependents; VACUUM; compare file size | |
| QA-DEL-079 | `compaction` | Mark a model compacted that was never deleted | **refused (no_tombstone, 409)** | call `mark_compacted` for a live URN | not a missing resource — the wrong act |
| QA-DEL-080 | `compaction` | Mark a tombstone compacted twice | **refused (already_compacted, 409)** | mark; mark again | |
| QA-DEL-081 | `compaction` | Run a sweep as a non-administrator | **refused (403)** | authenticate without `admin` | |
| QA-DEL-082 | `compaction` | Add a new column holding a content address and sweep | **build fails** | add a digest column; run `tests/test_compaction.py` | a refcount is only a refcount if it counts every reference; a missed column marks a live blob and then deletes it |
| QA-DEL-083 | `compaction` | Sweep against a store directory that does not exist | **accepted; reports zero** | point at a missing root; sweep | must not report "nothing to reclaim" in a way indistinguishable from a store it could not read |
| QA-DEL-084 | `compaction` | Confirm `.partial` upload files are never marked | **accepted; skipped** | leave a `.partial` in the store; sweep twice | an upload in progress is not an orphan |
